cases.given: A move has startup/active/recovery and a 120 ms legal-next-action buffer.
cases.when: Attempt allowed and forbidden cancels; submit next actions 119, 120 and 121 ms before eligibility.
then: Only declared cancels occur.
With a half-open buffer [0,120), 119 ms-old input executes once; 120/121 ms-old input expires.

cases.given: One attack hit group overlaps several hurtboxes on one target.
cases.when: Deliver the same contact repeatedly and in reversed collider order.
then: Exactly one defense outcome and one damage/posture transaction occur for the attack/hit-group/target key.

cases.given: The same semantic attack is available through each supported input adapter.
cases.when: Replay the same action sequence through each adapter.
then: Combat events match; button labels may differ; no adapter has separate damage or defense rules.

cases.given: An adult has completed a tutorial and three graybox bouts.
cases.when: Ask for threat recognition, reasons for hits, alternative responses and replay interest.
then: Record actual answers and 1-5 readability/responsiveness scores.
Do not report fun or acceptance from unit-test success.

cases.given: Standard parry profile; eligible front strike; guard held; sufficient resource; an unused press at t=1000 ms.
cases.when: Resolve separate fixtures at contact ages -1, 0, 79, 80, 179, 180 and 181 ms.
then: No retroactive parry at -1.
Perfect at 0 and 79; ordinary parry at 80 and 179; guard fallback at 180 and 181.
Each fixture emits exactly one outcome.

cases.given: A valid parry window and front-cone limit of 60 degrees.
cases.when: Test angles 59.9, 60 and 60.1 degrees, plus rear attacks, blockable-only strikes and unblockable/unparryable strikes.
then: Eligible contacts at 59.9 and 60 can parry; 60.1 and rear contacts cannot.
Blockable-only strikes can block when guard rules allow; unblockable/unparryable strikes cannot block or parry.

cases.given: One accepted press at t=1000 ms; release required; 300 ms rearm interval.
cases.when: Hold with key-repeat, release/repress at 1299, and separately release/repress at 1300; deliver two contacts during one window.
then: Hold/repeat and the 1299 press do not rearm.
A released-and-pressed input at 1300 may rearm.
One press produces at most one parry; duplicates do not issue extra counters.

cases.given: Standard and assisted profiles are selectable independently of avatar and learner settings.
cases.when: Compare a contact at age 220 ms, then switch avatar without changing assistance.
then: Standard falls back to valid guard; assisted can ordinary-parry.
Avatar switching does not change timing settings or learner records.

cases.given: The enemy alternates a slow parryable strike and a visibly distinct dodge-required strike.
cases.when: Compare deliberate timing, held guard and repeated tapping in recorded adult trials.
then: Record success, damage and mistaken cue interpretations per strategy.
Do not promote the design if repeated tapping dominates deliberate play or threat types remain confusing.

cases.given: An assisted story profile with simple tap controls, auto-shield and recoverable bonk/revive.
cases.when: Complete the encounter without performing a successful timed parry.
then: Story progress and rewards remain obtainable without precision timing, held-button skill or reading during combat.
A failed attempt does not cause story game over or erase earned progress.

cases.given: A counter opportunity starts at t=1000 and expires at t=1600 ms.
cases.when: Attempt independent counters at 1599 and 1600; replay a consumed opportunity ID.
then: 1599 is eligible, 1600 is expired, and a consumed ID cannot execute again.

cases.given: An enemy is just below its posture-break threshold.
cases.when: Apply the crossing event twice, then more hits during the same break.
then: One break transition is emitted for that crossing.
Duplicated events do not extend the break or grant repeated rewards.

cases.given: A counter target resolves or becomes invalid before consumption.
cases.when: Press counter and switch targets.
then: The stale opportunity is rejected or explicitly cancelled; no teleport, crash or inherited counter against another enemy.

cases.given: The same opening permits a counterattack or escape.
cases.when: Ask a tester to use both, then face an enemy with a declared break-resistance rule.
then: Both choices are understandable and executable.
Record infinite-stagger attempts and whether resistance is explained by observable feedback.

cases.given: A dragon with a defined local forward defense arc.
cases.when: Pitch and roll it through several orientations; test equivalent local-front and local-rear incoming vectors.
then: Equivalent local angles produce equivalent eligibility; roll/pitch do not accidentally grant a global shield.

cases.given: One eligible bolt crosses multiple dragon hurt zones during a single step.
cases.when: Deflect it and replay the contact/event; test immediate overlap with the new owner.
then: One ownership change and one reflection occur.
No immediate self-hit or reflection recursion occurs.

cases.given: A reflectable bolt, a nonreflectable sustained beam and an area blast approach the dragon.
cases.when: Use defend, evade and the chosen counter path in separate trials.
then: Only the declared bolt can reflect; other threats follow their explicit rules.
The selected reflection/return-aim policy is documented and observed.

cases.given: The three-drone flight arena with a selectable target and brake/turn assistance.
cases.when: Ask an adult tester to pursue, defend and re-engage; destroy the locked target during a separate trial.
then: Record time spent reacquiring versus engaging, control confusion and discomfort.
Destroyed targets release safely; progression does not require advanced manual roll control.

cases.given: One sortie with shared progress and Cadet/Pilot/Ace assistance profiles.
cases.when: Switch tiers mid-sortie; exercise declared stall, terrain-contact and wing-energy recovery cases.
then: Progress, rewards and cooldowns persist across tier changes.
Cadet does not demand independent pitch/yaw/roll/throttle/camera control; declared assistance prevents fatal collision.
No tier crashes the dragon fatally; recovery follows the recorded profile rather than deleting progress.

cases.given: Cadet and Pilot versions of the same flight-school and bounded dogfight scene on the selected input device.
cases.when: Perform banked turns, climbs, throttle/boost changes and a pursuit/reversal; compare atmosphere and assisted-space profiles.
then: Record whether speed, banking, momentum and turning communicate fighter-jet feel rather than corridor-only steering.
The chosen profile documents its energy/stall/assist policy; advanced controls are not required for the Cadet test.

cases.given: A one-token high-threat encounter with three enemies.
cases.when: Request attacks simultaneously, then cancel, resolve and despawn the current token holder in separate fixtures.
then: At most one high-threat attack is committed at a time.
The token is released on every exit path and another enemy can act.

cases.given: An enemy has declared wind-up, target-commitment and recovery intervals.
cases.when: Move across its aim before and after commitment; interrupt it before the active phase.
then: Tracking follows the declared policy rather than snapping late.
An interrupted attack cannot later deal a ghost hit.

cases.given: A high-threat enemy begins outside the camera view.
cases.when: Trigger its warning and attack while a tester engages a visible enemy.
then: A directional non-text-only warning or delayed attack gives a meaningful response opportunity.
Record reaction/cue failures; no readability pass is inferred from the event log alone.

cases.given: A seeded encounter or boss phase transition and a recorded input trace.
cases.when: Replay it twice and cross a phase threshold during an attack.
then: State/event traces match for the same seed and inputs.
Phase policy explicitly finishes or cancels the attack without duplicated damage or unexplained invulnerability.

cases.given: A fast projectile crosses a thin hurtbox between adjacent simulation positions.
cases.when: Run the declared sweep/continuous-contact test and report repeated contact callbacks.
then: The crossing is detected once; repeated callbacks do not duplicate the combat transaction.

cases.given: A two-hit move has two explicit hit-group IDs and the target has overlapping hurtboxes.
cases.when: Deliver both groups repeatedly.
then: Exactly two intended hit transactions occur, one per group, not one per collider.

cases.given: A target is occluded, destroyed or out of selection range; a wall obstructs the follow camera.
cases.when: Lock, cycle targets, move toward the wall and remove the target.
then: The documented occlusion policy is applied; invalid locks clear safely.
The camera does not remain inside geometry or snap to an arbitrary distant target.

cases.given: An identical input trace with effects on, reduced motion on, and effects off.
cases.when: Replay all three settings with the same simulation step and seed.
then: Combat state and outcomes match.
Presentation differences do not change damage, parry eligibility or counter expiry.

cases.given: A fixed-step combat simulation, seeded scene and timestamped input recording.
cases.when: Render the same replay at 30, 60 and 120 FPS with one injected rendering stall.
then: The combat event/state sequence matches across render schedules.
Any time clamping policy is explicit; no silent skipped damage or extra parries.

cases.given: A held guard, buffered action and active counter opportunity.
cases.when: Lose focus, suspend the tab and resume after a long gap.
then: Held/buffered input is safely cleared; no catch-up burst or stuck control occurs.
Counter expiry follows the documented paused-simulation policy.

cases.given: The single-player graybox scene with an optional service unavailable.
cases.when: Perform attack, dodge, parry and counter with network access blocked.
then: Immediate local combat still resolves; any save/sync error is reported separately.
This test does not claim multiplayer correctness.

cases.given: A named real device/browser/input combination and a fixed scene/build/profile.
cases.when: Record performance and control trials with assistance and reduced motion toggled.
then: Store actual p50/p95/p99 frame times, input latency method, sample duration and failures.
No device PASS without that device being exercised and an agreed budget.
Assistance changes do not mutate learner identity or mastery records.

cases.given: Two party members in a separately authorized later prototype.
cases.when: Switch leader while movement/guard is held.
then: Exactly one actor receives direct control; old held actions and invalid references are cleared.

cases.given: One parry-linked assist opportunity with a unique ID.
cases.when: Trigger the assist repeatedly and switch leader before replaying the ID.
then: At most one assist transaction is granted; switching cannot duplicate it.

cases.given: A leader and follower separated by an obstacle.
cases.when: Move, stop and return through a narrow passage.
then: The declared catch-up policy avoids permanent blocking or uncontrolled repeated teleporting.
A failure is recorded, not hidden by disabling the obstacle.

cases.given: A two-member scene with one clearly signaled optional assist.
cases.when: Ask an adult tester to fight, switch leader and use or ignore the assist.
then: Record whether support is understandable without extra micromanagement.
No multiplayer, all-five-character or split-party completion claim follows from this test.

cases.given: One valid alley-oop with a setter, finisher and setter cooldown; result is committed on finish resolution.
cases.when: Double-tap, pause during apex slow motion, switch avatar mid-air, and separately skip/reduce/interrupt presentation.
then: Exactly one finish result and the declared setter cooldown are applied; launch alone does not prematurely apply the final result.
Presentation variants preserve the resolved outcome; auto-finish and explicit tap cannot both cash in the same launch.

cases.given: An enemy can carry one main status plus Exposed, with simulation-time expiry.
cases.when: Apply competing main statuses and Exposed; pause across the expiry time, then resume.
then: The declared replacement/stacking policy keeps at most one main status plus Exposed.
Pause freezes remaining duration; status expires once after the remaining active simulation time.

cases.given: A phase has earned items, removed sparks and already resolved enemies.
cases.when: Bonk all family members and resume the phase.
then: Earned items, removed sparks and resolved enemies remain accounted for.
The family recovers without story game over or duplicated awards; assistance is offered without penalty.

cases.given: Enemies have targets, including one family member who becomes bonked or begins reviving.
cases.when: Retarget and resolve pending attacks.
then: Bonked/reviving members are not selected or hit by stale targeted attacks.
A valid safe alternative or idle behavior is used.

cases.given: Active setter/ability cooldowns and a component reward keyed by stable ID.
cases.when: Switch avatar, pause/resume, reload mid-fight and repeat the reward/tandem trigger.
then: Cooldowns do not reset and the component is awarded once.
No extra Family Spark is generated by replay, reload or avatar switching alone.

cases.given: An alley-oop can launch the player or a companion and has an automatic finish.
cases.when: Trigger once with no second tap; remove the target at the apex; test player-as-setter and player-as-finisher.
then: One safe automatic finish occurs, using the declared area fallback when the target is gone.
No failed landing or required perfect timing; the result is applied once.

cases.given: Five member IDs with shared LaunchDefinition and FinisherDefinition records.
cases.when: Enumerate distinct ordered setter/finisher pairs; trigger after avatar switching while the setter is on cooldown.
then: Exactly 20 distinct non-self pairs are valid, without requiring 20 bespoke implementations.
Setter cooldown persists through avatar switching; no status setup is required for a valid basic alley-oop.
